newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-ROSSET INJURY HANDS VICTORY TO SOUTH AFRICA.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-ROSSET INJURY HANDS VICTORY TO SOUTH AFRICA.

text.p: Marc Rosset started the year on sad note when he was forced to retire with a back injury from Wednesday's Hopman Cup clash with South Africa to all but end the Swiss team's run in the mixed-teams event.

Rosset, wearing a back brace, looked set to steer the second seeds to a comfortable victory in their Group B tie after teenager Martina Hingis had easily disposed of Amanda Coetzer 6-1 6-2 in under an hour.
The tall right-hander was in command of his match against world number 10 Wayne Ferreira, leading 6-0 2-0 when he collided with a ball girl at the net and fell to the court clutching his back.
Rosset's career has been plagued by back injuries and he further damaged muscles around a lower disc during practice on Saturday.
He forfeited his opening singles tie to Romania's Adrian Voinea on Monday, but managed to play the mixed doubles with Hingis to secure a 2-1 victory.
Rosset had said his goal in 1997 was to make it through the year injury-free after a wretched run which saw him suffer a broken foot in 1995 and a broken finger last year.
He missed the 1996 Australian Open when he hurt his hand after smashing an advertising hoarding in a fit of rage during last year's Hopman Cup final against Croatia.

Ferreira had no answer to Rosset's array of ground strokes on Wednesday and only managed to win his first service game when the injured Swiss player failed to make any serious attempt to chase the South African's shots.
He received further treatment courtside during the break between games but forfeited the match when he realised he could not even toss the ball for his serve.

Tournament director Paul McNamee said he was unsure whether Rosset would be fit to play in Switzerland's last group match against Germany on Friday, but was confident he would be okay for next week's Sydney tournament and the Australian Open starting on January 13.
"I would expect him to play in Melbourne given the information I've got from medical staff," said McNamee, who is also tournament director for the Grand Slam event.
South Africa only need to beat newcomers Romania on Friday to secure their first final berth in the eight-team tournament.
The two unbeaten teams in Group A, Croatia and the United States, meet later on Wednesday.
